description: Where a recipe-plan genre's pieces go (P9j.core-build-plan, operator ruling U103(3); GAP-TOOL5). anchors = genreBuildAnchors(world, {course, puzzle}): tables from atom to value, in code-unit key order, an atom two entries give different values being null (ambiguous): places (Course.places → {x, z}), links (traversalLinkId → {from, to}), containers (worldAtom(id) → its position, else its building's lot), locks (lock → target), clues (clue → the first lock that needs it), businesses (worldAtom(name) → its lot, else its first building's lot), settlements (worldAtom(name) → position), people (worldAtom(first last) → the NPC schedule's home lot, else the first building listing them as occupant). place = placeGenrePieces(genre, pieces, anchors): each piece in input order is checked (invalid-piece, duplicate-id, unknown-kind incl. a kind of another module, kind-not-placed, invalid-variant), keeps a stamped archetype or carries its derived key, then stands at an authored position (invalid-position) or by its kind's placement rule (GENRE_PIECE_PLACEMENT: steps in order, a step whose field the piece lacks skipped, a missing atom falling through to the next step, a null one stopping as ambiguous-anchor; when all fall through, the first step's missing-anchor with its table and atom; when none applies, no-anchor); locks and clues follow on to their container; a gap stands at its link's midpoint with span {from, to}. Pieces an anchor puts on one point are settled: the first stays, the n-th next moves by genreBuildSettleOffset(n); gaps and authored positions never move. Only an unknown genre is refused. plan = genreBuildPlan(genre, world, definitions): genrePiecesFor (its refusals), then the world's own entities.genrePieces (input order), placed together over anchors: a world piece of a kind the definitions derive, in a module the genre places, is the plan's own (recomputed and not read; reported not-derived, after every other report, when the definitions no longer derive its id); every other world piece is the assistant's and is placed like any other (a piece with an at loses any position first, so it is re-placed from its anchor; one sharing a derived id is a duplicate-id). settle = genreBuildSettleOffset(n). ground = genreBuildGround(genre, world, definitions) (PL.core-recipe-plan-ground, operator ruling U116(2)): plan's answer {genre, ground, pieces, unplaced} (its refusals), where ground holds, for each module of ground.modules the genre places (platformer, puzzle), a GenreGroundIR {id <module>.ground.<course|puzzle>, module, kind ground, ref course|puzzle, archetype prop.<module>.ground, position the extent's midpoint, extent {min, max}}: the rectangle over every point an anchor placed one of the module's pieces on, once settled (an authored position never widens it), widened by ground.marginM metres on each side, its top the IR ground plane; none when no piece of the module was placed by an anchor. Every placed piece of a grounded module stands on its ground (edges included) or is left out and reported off-ground, after every report of the plan; pieces of other modules (strategy) are as plan placed them. The world's own entities.genreGround is never read. write = writeGenreBuildPlan(world, that grounded plan), answered as {genrePieces, genreGround} of the written world (or the refusal): the placed pieces, then the assistant's pieces the plan left out (a collectible, block or switch with a string ref, string optional fields and an id not already written) as its id, module, kind, ref, variant, at, level and archetype only (no position), then the ground as entities.genreGround. Numbers compare exactly: no position is rounded or computed with trigonometry.
sources: The plan: src/genre-systems/build-plan.ts (genreBuildAnchors, GENRE_PIECE_PLACEMENT, placeGenrePieces, genreBuildSettleOffset, genreBuildPlan, genreBuildGround, writeGenreBuildPlan); the pieces it places: src/genre-systems/genre-pieces.ts (genrePiecesFor, genrePieceId) and conformance/genre-pieces/kinds.json; the ground's shape: genreGroundIrSchema in src/schemas/world-ir.schema.ts.

Fixtures: Thistlecombe's world from conformance/genre-mechanics/thistlecombe.world-slice.json, cut to what the anchors read; its course, puzzle and campaign generated from it exactly as the first cases of conformance/platformer/course.json, conformance/puzzle/definition.json and conformance/strategy/campaign.json pin them, with only the members a piece or an anchor is derived from. The rest written in src/genre-systems/build-plan-corpus-cases.ts.
comparison: exact, numbers included, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent); an input value {"$fixture": name} is the file's fixture of that name; an unknown op is an error, never a skip
